utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We try again. If the witness could be brought in. While that is happening, I will mention three matters. In November the Chamber ordered the Defence to disclose three of its expert reports by the 18th of January. One of those has been disclosed only in B/C/S so far, and the delay is in obtaining a translation into English. I understand that will be done this week. Because of that, the Chamber is prepared to extend until the 5th of March the requirement that the Prosecution give its notice under Rule 94(B). That's in respect of that one report only. There was a motion of the Prosecution regarding Exhibit 509, and that will be granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was also a motion of Mr. Djordjevic's Defence regarding Exhibit 217. The Chamber will grant leave to the Defence to upload the missing two pages to Exhibit D217. The Chamber also notes that the English translation currently in e-court appears to be a draft rather than a final translation. When a final translation is available, the Defence should replace the draft with the official translation. And now, sir, we welcome you this morning. Would you be so kind as to stand and read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Mr. Djurdjic has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I just ask you two things before we start with the testimony of this witness. First, the exhibit D452 marked for identification in the e-court under D010-5382, could it please be admitted into evidence because the translation has been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The only procedural difficulty, Mr. Djurdjic, is that our number in e-court is different from the D010-5382 that you quote. MFI D452 will become Exhibit D452, and you can sort out the precise number later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just a question of numbers for the Serbian and English versions. One further thing, last week we asked for our 65 ter list to be extended for the number 1791. So could that be allowed too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will deal with that later, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you please introduce yourself and give us your particulars.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zivadin Jovanovic. I was born in 1938 in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to briefly inform you of the summary -- of the summary of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness in the period from 1998 until the year 2000 was the minister for foreign affairs in the Government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. He will testify about the activities of Yugoslav diplomacy in the context of attempts of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia to deal with the problem of Kosovo and Metohija by peaceful and political means. He will testify about the efforts of the federal government to enable foreign diplomatic representatives to familiarise themselves on the spot with the actual state of affairs in Kosovo and Metohija and also to facilitate their work on the ground. For that reason, in Kosovo and Metohija offices were opened within the framework of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to provide logistic support to foreign diplomatic representatives. As the federal minister of foreign affairs, the witness signed an agreement with Bronislaw Geremek, who at the time was the chairman of the OSCE on the establishment of a Kosovo Verification Mission. The federal government formed a special body for co-operation with the OSCE, a commission of the federal government for co-operation with the Kosovo Verification Mission. The tasks of that commission were to establish contact and co-operation with the verification mission, and primarily with the leaders of that mission. The witness will confirm that the federal government, the commission, and all the ministries had a positive attitude towards the verification mission, their aim being to seriously review and deal with all the requests of the verification mission wherever possible. The witness will confirm that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, I really am. I didn't realise my friend was going to embark on reading a very long summary of what is in the previous testimony of the witness, which is not yet received. Now, I will have no objection to the application to tender the evidence, the previous evidence, on a Rule 92 ter -- as a matter of fact, I think the Court has already approved the -- or granted the submission, but I think the practice has been and the proper way is that the statement or the 92 ter transcript should be brought before the Court and formally become part of the evidence before we read the summary. It might well just be a procedural point, but I don't know if it's right to be reading the factual contents without the statement being put before the Court and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber does agree with Mr. Stamp, Mr. Djurdjic, that it would be more convenient and appropriate to receive the statement as an exhibit and then to receive a summary of it. It may in most cases be a matter of mere form, but there are cases where that can be an issue of some significance. So we will follow that procedure. You tender this previous transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I reviewed the transcript during the Prosecution case, and the procedure was as I am doing now, so that is why I started without asking leave of the Chamber. I realise now how we will work in the future, so I will ask for the transcript to be admitted first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Our recollection of the procedure before is a little different, Mr. Djurdjic, but no matter. The transcript of evidence of the witness in the previous trial is evidence having been given on the 20th and 21st of August, 2007, will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two versions, a revised and a non-revised version. So the transcript under seal D101-3359 should be admitted into evidence, please. And the revised and non-revised version, the number being D011-0768.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is merely a redacted or edited version; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was dealing with the primary document. It first will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the statement will be given Exhibit Number D00454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the redacted statement will also be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that statement will be Exhibit D00455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now your summary which was interrupted, Mr. Djurdjic, may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another technical matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, you remember and you read the transcript of the statement you made in the Milutinovic case on the 20th and 21st of August, 2007. Would you today provide the same answers to the same questions that you were asked then?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness during his testimony will also convey his knowledge about the withdrawal of the forces of the Army of Yugoslavia and the MUP after the signing of the agreement on the establishment of the KVM led to the intensified -- intensification of activities of the Kosovo forces and the capture of territory by the Kosovo forces which had been abandoned by the forces of Serbia and Yugoslavia. The witness will speak about the negotiations in Rambouillet and will explain that the agreement was never fully disclosed to the Yugoslav and Serbian side, and the delegation that was led by Professor Ratko Markovic had the authority to reach an agreement with a view to dealing with the crisis by political means. The federal ministry had a team of experts in diplomacy, law, and other areas who provided logistic support to the delegations in Rambouillet and Paris. The witness will testify that the policy of the federal government and the Government of the Republic of Serbia advocated the resolution of the problems in Kosovo by peaceful means, and this policy remained unchanged in 1998 and 1999, including the Milutinovic-Rugova Agreement which envisaged the possibility of forming a provisional government for Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, could you tell us what your educational background is.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: By education, I'm a jurist; and by profession, I'm a diplomat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether your years of service were spent mostly in the diplomacy.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in the diplomatic service from 1994 until -- I'm sorry, from 1964 until the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in 1998 and 1999 what position you held?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was federal minister for foreign affairs from January 1998 until December 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, could you tell us briefly what was the status of the republics within the Federation, the legal and political status of the republics from the standpoint of foreign policy of the Yugoslav Federation in the 1998/1999 period, and how those policies were formed and implemented.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was, by its constitution, had a unique and uniform foreign policy, whereas the members of the Yugoslav Federation by constitution took part in creating and carrying out that single foreign policy of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, at the federal level which actors influenced the policy making and what was the task of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: By constitution of the FRY, the responsibility for policy making and carrying out foreign policy of the federal state was in the hands of the federal government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Other -- others who had a hand in creating foreign policy were the constitutional bodies, the Federal Assembly of the FRY and the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And the division of competencies and responsibilities in creating and carrying out of foreign policy are written in the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us how republics took part in creating the foreign policy at the federal level?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, when it comes to the federal government it comprised representatives of the republics, members of the Federation; and in that respect, each republic through the federal government took part in conducting foreign policy. Furthermore, republics also had a constitutionally laid-down number in -- of delegates or deputies in the Federal Assembly, and to the extent that the Federal Assembly had a role in creating and carrying out foreign policy of Yugoslavia, to that extent those deputies influenced such creation in carrying out foreign policy in the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, who had the constitutional role of carrying out the determined single foreign policy of federal Yugoslavia, minister was from one republic and the deputy minister was from the other member of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back, please, since Federation is a composite state, who had the international entity, the member republics or the federal republic?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The sovereignty was with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia exclusively, and only the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was an actor in international relations with other states and with international organisations. Republics could take part in certain contacts at international level, but exclusively in the carrying out of foreign policy when it's related to the immediate, direct interests of the said republic member of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Kosovo and Metohija autonomous province was within which republic? It was a constituent part of which republic?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Kosovo and Metohija had always been an integral part of the Republic of Serbia. To wit, the Republic of Serbia by all the constitutions from World War II to date has had two provinces, one was Kosovo and Metohija and the other one was Vojvodina. It would be interesting to note that the Kosovo and Metohija autonomous province during World War II changed names and competencies. Immediately after the World War II it was an autonomous district within Serbia. Later on it became autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In terms of foreign policy, terrorism which had in Kosovo and Metohija, was it an internal affair of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, or was it an international issue?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: For many years -- many decades, Serbia had been facing separatist tendencies in Kosovo and Metohija. And in the 1980 and 1990s, those separatist tendencies worked hand in hand with terrorism. So leaders of the separatist movement in Kosovo and Metohija growingly used terrorism as means for achieving political -- their political goal, and that would be for that part of Serbia to secede from the rest of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to slow down because of the transcript and to make a pause between question and answer. Mr. Jovanovic, what was the international position of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the end of 1997 and the beginning of 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was complex for several reasons, the basic reason being why the position of the FRY at that time was so complex was the suspension of its membership rights within the UN system, the OSCE system, and in many other international organisations. The second element why it was so complex is reflected in the fact that despite the decision of the Security Council of the UN dated end of 1995, after the conclusion of the Dayton-Paris accords on peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina, stipulating that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is to see the sanctions introduced in May 1992 lifted. Despite all that, the US of A as key international actor continued contravening UN Security Council's decision to maintain the out of all -- the so-called out of all of the sanctions. Complexity lie also in the fact that a substantial part of the FRY's borders - and I mean the borders of Serbia, Kosovo and Metohija towards Albania - its integrity was infringed by the influx of arms after the well-known events in Albania, meaning arms went into Serbia or Kosovo and Metohija. Complexity also was reflected in the fact that Yugoslavia had inherited substantial economic and financial debts and losses due to a long period of isolation and sanctions. So that was the position of the FRY which prompted all its institutions to invest great efforts to -- into overcoming the consequences of the isolation and sanctions which were still in force contrary to UN Security Council's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've just mentioned that those sanctions sponsored by the US of A, the so-called out of all of the sanctions remained in force. I would like to ask you in practical terms what the out of all of sanctions was, what consequences it had on the FRY?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The sanctions had -- the so-called out of all of sanctions influenced or resulted in a very dire economic and social situation in Yugoslavia. Yugoslavia did not have any opportunity to withdraw or draw down loans from international financial institutions, first and foremost from the IMF and the World Bank or from European financial institutions. Yugoslavia could not take part in free trade without restrictions, whereby the principle of free trade and open borders was being violated. This had consequences on our insufficient utilisation of industrial capacities in Yugoslavia. They went idle because important raw materials could not be imported for the dearth of financial resources. We had very low foreign exchange influx into the country and this directly resulted in reduced manufacture of pharmaceuticals, for instance, because despite the fact that Yugoslavia was a rare example of a country in that region to produce large quantities of pharmaceuticals, but since it could not import the raw materials, the chemicals, that had an effect that Yugoslavia which had been a net exporter of pharmaceuticals, now faced a situation where it could not meet its own demand -- domestic demand for pharmaceuticals.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You just stated that the Republic of Yugoslavia was excluded from certain international organisations. Could you please tell us, are we discussing the SFRY or the FRY, how it was excluded from certain international organisations, and which organisations those were.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have to be very precise and specific about this matter. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had never been excluded from any international organisation, had never been a decision on cessation of FRY's membership in any international organisation, including the UN and the system of the United Nations, international financial institutions and co-operations, the OSCE, and others. After the destruction of the SFRY, what was inherited by the FRY was the suspension of membership rights, provisional suspension of membership rights from those international organisations I mentioned a minute ago. So SFRY was suspended from the membership of the OSCE at the beginning of the 1990s when the Yugoslav crisis broke out. In a very peculiar way that was done too. Ever since its establishment to date, in principle the OSCE decisions are taken by consensus of all the member states. At the beginning of the 1990s, the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was suspended. It was not thrown out. It was suspended provisionally through an imposition of an ad hoc principle of consensus minus one, and this was the only case in the history of the OSCE where the principle of consensus was not upheld. Otherwise, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as one of the successors of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia has always considered itself as, in terms of continuity, as being a member of the United Nations, the OSCE, and all the other international organisations, not only that. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia co-operated with those organisations, had a very positive attitude towards those organisations throughout that period. It had a positive attitude to all initiatives and requests coming from those organisations. As far as membership in the UN is concerned, the decision was to suspend Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's right to participation at the General Assembly. Later on in the EKOSOK and later on in other parts of that systems, the system of the United Nations. But throughout that time while the FRY was suspended, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was allowed to maintain its permanent missions to both New York and Geneva headquarters of the UN, and to use those missions to continue to build contacts and co-operation up to the level it was allowed to do so. FRY maintained continuous diplomatic communication with the heads of the United Nations, the OSCE, and all the other international organisations, and it met its financial obligation towards those organisations in terms of membership fees. I personally on two occasions during -- at General Assemblies of the UN, I personally handed to the Secretary-General of the United Nations cheques to cover the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia 's contribution to the finances of the UN. Both times it was construed as a positive gesture at a time when there were many UN member states and some international organisations who were not in such dire economic circumstances, that were not under sanctions, that were not isolated, but who failed promptly to honour their financial contributions towards international organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, could you please tell us what was the internal political situation like in the spring of 1998 in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The social and economic situation throughout that period was complicated. The deficit in the payments and trade balances, there was a deficit with respect to many needs and commodities required for the normal functioning of a state and society. However, with something that was of the utmost importance for assessing the internal stability and the situation at home, was the rather abrupt increase of terrorist activities of the so-called KLA in the province of Kosovo and Metohija. There were certain social tensions, but the economic or the difficult social situation did not affect the overall internal situation as much as did the sudden escalation of terrorism of the so-called KLA in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the aim of these terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I have already pointed out, the key problem, the basic issue, and the root cause of the problems in Kosovo and Metohija was the long-term strategy of separatist forces in Kosovo and Metohija, the aim of which was for a long period of time the secession of Kosovo and Metohija from Serbia, that is, from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell us as far as you know what those terrorist activities consisted of.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The separatism was reflected in many areas and primarily the separatist leadership in Kosovo and Metohija boycotted the constitutional order, the legal order, and the state which Kosovo and Metohija belonged to. The boycott consisted of failure to participate in elections, non-participation in other activities initiated by Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, a boycott in the educational area, boycotting the system of health care and education, and other institutions and state functions as well as the formation of illegal counter-constitutional parallel institutions by the separatist leadership, or rather, bodies of a separatist nature. This separatist organisation and the leaders of separatism in that period of time resorted to many measures of intimidation, threats, blackmail, and even revenge against compatriots of Albanian ethnicity who would in any way whatsoever express loyalty towards the state in which they were citizens. Along those lines of separatism, a wave of terrorist activity escalated so that certain political aims, such as the secession of Kosovo and Metohija from Serbia were pursued by terrorist means. How did this terrorism manifest itself? In many ways and in many areas, but primarily it was directed against the legitimate representatives of the authorities against everything that represented the state, its institutions, and the overall constitutional system. There were many attacks and assassinations and killings of policemen, soldiers, and other members of public services such as, for instance, teachers in schools that were part of the legal and legitimate educational system, foresters who were wearing state uniforms, postmen who were also uniformed wearing postal service uniforms. So there were attacks against civilians as well, and not only against members of the Serbian people but also against members of the Albanian national minority who as I have mentioned showed loyalty. An atmosphere was being created in which no one dared to be loyal to the state of which he was a citizen. And, if I may be allowed to mention, all this was not just running counter to the valid constitutional and legal system, not only was it in contravention in the rule of law, but it was also contrary to the Convention of the Council of Europe on the rights of members of ethnic minorities which contains a provision saying that the rights of ethnic minorities do not reduce the obligation of members of ethnic minorities to be loyal to the state in which they are citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just ask in connection with this issue, regardless of such a situation in Kosovo and Metohija did all the inhabitants avail themselves of their collective rights in respect of pensions, social benefits, and contributions, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Even in the case of Kosovo and Metohija, the boycott of the institutions of the system, the boycott of the legal system, and the formation of illegal and parallel institutions with separatist goals was implemented selectively to a certain degree. Namely, no member of the Albanian ethnic minority and members of any other ethnic communities in Kosovo and Metohija did not renounce their pensions, social benefits, and other benefits provided by the state. When we talk about a boycott, it applied in the first place to boycotting the institutions of the authorities, of the state authorities, a boycott of legal local self-government, a boycott of the police, the educational system. But this did not go so far as to anyone renouncing or being forced to denounce his rights to any material or financial benefit provided on the basic of the principle that applied to all the citizens of Serbia or Yugoslavia by the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we give the witness a hard copy of the documents to facilitate their use?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I will now give you the number of the tab in which you will find the document. Could you please open the binder so as -- so that you can turn the pages more easily. Before we move on to the first document, Mr. Jovanovic, let me ask you, this situation in Kosovo and Metohija, how did it affect the movement of goods and services and of people in Kosovo and Metohija and the functioning of the economy in general?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you are referring to 1998, then it should be noted that in the spring, that is, early that year, the terrorist KLA virtually had control using armed means of a considerable part of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, a territory which in legal and political terms was an integral part of the Republic of Serbia, and thereby also an integral part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. In a considerable part of the territory of Serbia in Kosovo and Metohija, there was no freedom of movement. There was no freedom -- free traffic or circulation of goods and people or any other elements because those parts of the territory were under -- were by force of arms under the control of the so-called KLA. This affected the overall atmosphere, the economy, the normal life and work of citizens of Serbia in Kosovo and Metohija and, on the other hand, this raised major problems for the authorities of Serbia and the Republic of Yugoslavia, whose obligation it was to ensure the normal traffic, normal functioning of the economy and public services such as the educational and health care systems, public security, freedom of movement of citizens, et cetera. In those days, in a large part of the territory of Serbia, in Kosovo and Metohija there were barricades, check-points, which prevented the normal functioning of social and economic life and which disrupted the unity of authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now look at document -- document number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have document D008-5801.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm wondering if we could get the Defence 65 ter number. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. 65 ter it is 1264, document 1264.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, could you comment on this document and tell us what political issues it deals with.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Document number 1.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. In a -- the situation that I have illustrated, the questions facing the political leadership of Serbia, of which Kosovo and Metohija is an integral part, was how to deal with the problems of Kosovo and Metohija. The strategy of addressing this problem can be understood from the declaration issued by the President of the Republic of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic, about the political process in Kosovo and Metohija, and this is the document we have before us. It is clearly stated in that document the public and consistent platform by the Republic of Serbia, of which Kosovo and Metohija is an integral part, for the problems in Kosovo and Metohija to be successfully resolved only if political dialogue were to be accepted without delay and without any previous conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at page 2 in the B/C/S and in English page 2 as well. Please discuss that part of the declaration which concerns international integrations.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It illustrates what has already been demonstrated, to wit that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as an actor in international relations accepts and commits itself to all the basic documents underpinning the international legal order, first and foremost the UN Charter, the final document of Helsinki, and the values enshrined in the Paris Charter. It reflects a constructive and positive attitude of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia towards all international organisations, particularly openness and interest for full normal co-operation with the OSCE which presumes the need to have its full membership rights restored in the OSCE, a precondition for which would be a cessation of the suspension of membership rights that had been imposed at the time by the implication of the principle of consensus minus one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please discuss the following paragraph about the education and the 3 plus 3 group, if you could expand on that.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In co-operation with the organisation of St. Egidio headed by Monsignor Palija, a group 3 plus 3 was established to carry out the agreement on the normalisation of education in Kosovo and Metohija, which meant that a single system of education had to be restored and put in place, which means that the parallel separatist educational system had to desist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the Albanian representatives take part in this process, did they join this process, and did they do their bit in restoring the educational system of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a specific issue, where as foreign minister I did not have any direct participation. But I was familiar with the agreement that had been reached on that, and I was briefed on a certain degree of progress in resolving this issue. To wit, at that time, despite the problems in the work in the 3 plus 3 group and despite certain obstructions, an increase in the number of members of the Albanian minority enrolling at the Prishtina University. That increase was significant and this is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The declaration of the 18th of March, 1998 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00456.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If we could please take a look at tab 2 for your benefit, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the OTP it would be 65 ter 966, and in e-court that would be D008-4250.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, here we have a request sent by the FRY to be admitted into the Council of Europe. You signed it on the 18th of March, 1998. Could you please comment this document from the perspective of the then-policy of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The main preoccupation, the focus of foreign policy of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, at the time when I was federal minister of foreign affairs, was to normalise the country's status in terms of membership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in international organisations. In the ministry that I headed, we saw that as an important, inevitable course that we had to take to take our country out of isolation, out of sanctions, and a course towards the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's taking responsibilities to help achieve those international organisations' goals. The document that I have before me is an illustration, an example of such policies and such direction that we took to overcome our isolation and to normalise the international standing and position of our country through the normalisation of its membership status. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on the 18th of March, 1998, submitted its official request for admission into the Council of Europe. And in this letter that I sent on behalf of the Government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the Secretary-General of the Council of Europe, first of all it is stated the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's desire to be admitted into the membership of the Council of Europe --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jovanovic. We can see that in the document.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you allow me, but what is evident in this document is that Yugoslavia by that time had ratified two key conventions of the Council of Europe, one on rights of members of ethnic minorities and the other on human rights. The document also demonstrates Yugoslavia's readiness and its capacity to contribute to the goals of the Council of Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version it appears there is a page which is in French which has no English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document from the Milutinovic case. The problem then was the same, and the solution is this: The first page of the document is a memo to the government, and then the rest is the French original of the document because the Council of Europe's official language is French. And it was not translated from one official language of this Court into another official language of this Court. And this is why this document remained in French. If you wish something else to be done then we can discuss it and try to see what we can do and about the Serbian translation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be preferable if you could obtain an English translation as well, and you are hereby authorised to include the English translation into the exhibit when you obtain it. That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00457.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to see the 65 ter document 960. That would be tab 3, Mr. Jovanovic. And the -- that would be D008-4223 in the e-court. Mr. Jovanovic, we are about to see a letter. I think that it is the document letter from Federal Government of the FRY to the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs with respect to the 76th Session concerning the initiative by the Yugoslav diplomacy from the 20th of March, 1998. I would like you to explain to us mechanisms of policy-making and what was the -- what were the methods of reporting back and forth between different bodies at the time while you were minister?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This document is one of many illustrations about how the federal government carried out its role as creator and executor of foreign policy. As a member of the cabinet, minister reports to the government and the government as the body which by constitution is in charge of conducting foreign policy, after such report issues instructions on how to proceed in terms of carrying out foreign policy and what should be done. In this case, the minister briefs the cabinet on what had been accomplished and receives from the cabinet, from the government, instructions on how to proceed further.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00458.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now please can we see document D008-5809. That would be 65 ter document 1266.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that would be tab 4, Mr. Jovanovic. It's on the screen. That would be Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs news bulletin dated 31st of March, 1998. Could you please comment this document in the light of the third and forth paragraph therein.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say is that this document illustrates the continuity of efforts by constitutional institutions of Serbia to launch the political process of resolving the issues in Kosovo and Metohija. After President Milutinovic's statement and declaration, the government which carries out policies, the Government of Serbia that is, accepts that and makes public their own opinion of the political process which is single and based on dialogue, based on European standards on human and civil rights, and based on a solution which would guarantee equal rights of all communities and citizens of Serbia in Kosovo and Metohija. This document also illustrates how Yugoslav diplomacy was being informed and briefed about those matters because this document was on the 31st of March -- was dispatched to all Yugoslav diplomatic and consular representative offices abroad which numbered more than 100 at the time. And this method of dissemination of information also testifies to the carrying out of single foreign policy when it comes to essential matters of peace, security, and the development of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00459.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I should now like to ask you to look at document number 5 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is Exhibit D1074 -- P, P, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, we have before us Resolution 1160 of the Security Council of the United Nations of the 31st of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you comment, please, on item 2 on page 2.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2 of the Security Council Resolution 1160 dated the 31st of March, 1998, calls upon the Kosovo Albanian leadership to condemn all terrorist action and that all elements in the Kosovo Albanian community should pursue their goals by peaceful means.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, are you aware whether terrorism was condemned by the Albanian political parties?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that the political leaderships and elements within the Albanian national community in Kosovo and Metohija never carried out this obligation stemming from the Security Council Resolution, not only that provided by this resolution but by many others in which the request for condemnation was repeated several times over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now comment on paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In item 5 the Security Council asserts the principles and proposals of the Contact Group of the 9th and 25th of March, 1998, and asserts the need for a political solution in Kosovo and Metohija with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Also, it points out that a solution to the Kosovo problems must be in accordance with the OSCE standards with the standards and principles of the Helsinki Final Act of 1975 and that any solution in Kosovo and Metohija must respect the principles, these principles, and must take into consideration the right of Albanians and all those living in Kosovo. The final request in that context and which is contained in this item of the Security Council Resolution is that a solution in Kosovo and Metohija must be reflected in an enhanced status of Kosovo within the territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge, was there any direct contact or negotiations between the Government of the Republic of Serbia and Yugoslavia and representatives of the political parties of Kosovo Albanians during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is clear from the previous document that the Government of the Republic of Serbia formed a delegation for negotiations on a peaceful political settlement in Kosovo and Metohija, and that that delegation was headed by the Vice-Premier of the Republic of Serbia, Professor Ratko Markovic. Representatives of those forces in Kosovo and Metohija which upheld separate tendencies refused to accept offers for a political dialogue with the legitimate representatives of the state, that is, with the delegation of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. We'll look at the next document and discuss this in somewhat greater detail. Could I ask you now to comment on item 8.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a request by the Security Council for an embargo on the import of weapons to the entire territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and therefore including Kosovo and Metohija as a part of the Republic of Serbia. This paragraph also calls on member states of the United Nations not to allow from their territories or using their flag vessels and aircraft for the transport of arms and ammunition, military vehicles, equipment, and spare parts, and this is also a call on all members of the United Nations to stop all activities linked to the arming, training, or financing of terrorist activities in this part of Serbia or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did the international community observe this request?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did but not in relation to Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you explain that a little, please.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This request of the Security Council for all UN member states to prevent the financing and arming and training of members of the terrorist KLA is repeated in virtually all Security Council Resolutions and in some resolutions the Security Council expresses its regret that this call, that this order, by the Security Council is not being implemented. It is ironic that this request for stopping arming, financing, and training of terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija was not respected even by certain permanent members of the Security Council, who had taken part in making this decision by the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just tell us which countries you're referring to in most cases that did not observe the -- these provisions.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, Germany. There was an influx of considerable funds from Germany for financing the so-called KLA. The president of the so-called government in exile of Kosovo and Metohija were Bukoshi. Throughout these terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija, he enjoyed the hospitality of the authorities of the Federal Republic of Germany. He had his own offices in several towns in the Federal Republic of Germany, through which frequently resorting to coercion and threat he collected taxes for what he called the liberation struggle in Kosovo and Metohija. This tax of several percentages was taken from every Albanian living and working in Germany. And even my ministry learnt of cases that this "tax" had to be paid even by Albanians who were receiving social benefits, unemployment benefits, in Germany. Our diplomacy, for instance, filed complaints on several occasions with the Ministry of Germany or we sent a demarche to the German embassy in Belgrade, requesting that the German government undertake appropriate measures to prohibit such illegal collection of funds on its territory, to prohibit the activities of illegal representatives whose aim is to jeopardise the constitutional order of a country which was a traditional partner of Germany's. The reaction was not appropriate. It is also quite well-known that weapons and some sophisticated equipment was obtained in the United States of America, which is a permanent member of the Security Council. There were no bans or efforts to prevent this from happening, even though Yugoslavia and the United States of America had the greatest contributions to achieving the peace agreement in Dayton. Nevertheless, there was a lack of will on the part of the US government to prevent the procurement of weapons and equipment in the United States of America for the needs of the so-called KLA in Kosovo and Metohija. Italy, Switzerland also failed to represent this ban. From Switzerland via Italy light weapons were sent to Kosovo for the terrorist KLA; from Turkey too we had information that weapons were provided. Great Britain, another permanent member of the Security Council, provided instructors for training members of the KLA. Such centres, training centres, were formed in the territory of Albania, in Tropoja and in a number of other places, the names of which I cannot recollect at this moment. The most important transit route for the import of weapons was Albanian, and via Albania the greatest part of the weapons arrived from these and other countries for the needs of the KLA. As for funds, the money was also collected in the United States of America, in Switzerland. Especially after Germany, Switzerland was also a country where considerable funds were collected. There were also certain criminal activities --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will have our first break now. The tapes will be rewound in 30 minutes, so we will resume at 11.05. An officer will assist you during the break, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: here

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see you, Mr. Djurdjic, signalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, until the witness comes in for the needs of the transcript, the unrevised transcript D454, could it be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There are private sessions in there, are there? Very well, for the moment it will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're continuing with Mr. Jovanovic, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, we were dealing with tab 6 in your binder. I would now like to ask you to move on to page 3 and to look at the end of paragraph 10. And if you could tell us briefly it says: "In this connection, the importance of the entering into force of the prohibitions imposed by this resolution stresses in this context the importance of implementation of the agreement on subregional arms control signed in Florence on the 14th of June, 1996." Could you briefly tell us what this agreement in Florence was about and what its significance is.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The agreement signed in Florence on the 14th of June, 1996, represents the implementation of the Dayton-Paris Agreement on peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This agreement on subregional arms control stipulated the proportions of heavy weapons that the three states of the former SFRY may have possession of, that is the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. This was a set of agreements that was signed at the time, and this set of agreements includes a protocol on inspection and supervision of the implementation and observance of the dead-lines and established proportions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in this item the UN Security Council calls on all parties for that agreement to be implemented further?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is important to note is that this agreement on the subregional arms control signed in June 1996, but that the UN Security Council re-affirms it through its resolution 1160 dated the 31st of March, 1998. Therefore, the UN Security Council de facto reminds everybody on the continuity of the validity and the need to implement that Florence Agreement dated 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at document 65 ter document 1267, e-court D008-5813.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that would be the next tab for you, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam O'Leary states 65 ter 1267 for the benefit of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, we have a statement by the President of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milutinovic, ahead of us. It was dated 7th of April, 1998. Could you please comment on paragraph 2 of this statement and what you know about that.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the previous document it is evident what the state leadership had invested in terms of efforts to launch the political process of resolving the problems in Kosovo and Metohija, particularly the efforts invested by the President of Serbia, Mr. Milan Milutinovic; the Serbian government's efforts; and the support that that process and that those efforts received from the federal level. This statement dated the 7th of April, 1998, issued by President Milutinovic in Pristina is another of those efforts, and it is evident from the paragraph that you mentioned that Kosmet Albanian representatives had not by that point accepted invitations to accede to political dialogue and to adopt political means for resolving the problems; rather, they had imposed conditions to that dialogue, thereby they deferred the process of political solution finding and continued de facto the tensions in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00460.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If we could please take a look at tab 7 for you, Mr. Jovanovic, 961 is the 65 ter number, and Exhibit D008-4226 in e-court. 4226, yes, that's correct. Mr. Jovanovic, we see here a document dated 7th of May, 1998. It is information by your ministry to the federal government concerning the opinion of the Contact Groups adopted in Rome on the 29th of April, 1998. Could you please tell us what was the government's assessment concerning the attitudes of the Contact Group in terms of their understanding of the Kosovo problems in connection with paragraph 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The federal government and Yugoslav diplomacy paid primary attention to the statements from the UN Security Council's resolution and conclusions and opinions of the Contact Group. This is another example illustrating that attention on the part of the federal government to the opinions of the Contact Group. In the report that I submitted at that government session, it was stated that the opinions of the Contact Group in connection with Kosovo and Metohija were at least in part biased, that they were not completely objective, where the responsibility for the deferral of political dialogue in Kosovo and Metohija is placed squarely and exclusively on the Serbian, that is, Yugoslav side, overlooking the fact that the representatives of the Albanian ethnic minority in Kosovo and Metohija had rejected many offers and calls on the part of constitutional institutions and organs of the Republic of Croatia [as interpreted] to launch political dialogue. The government stated that it had been surprised that attention is not being paid to the less-than-constructive attitudes of the representatives of the Albanian ethnic minority, who by rejecting political dialogue were sabotaging in effect the process of trying to find a political solution to the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can read about several efforts and initiatives to launch negotiations, to launch political dialogue. Why were they so adamant in rejecting such initiatives and such calls on the part of Albanian leadership?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I personally believe, and intelligence specific information hinted at that, that representatives of the Albanian ethnic minority did not accept any negotiations on a peaceful political solution because they predicted that that solution would be within the framework of Serbia and the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Yugoslavia when their real goal was secession. So representatives of the Albanian political structures from Kosovo and Metohija were not interested in any solution that would fall short of secession. And that -- and in that work they felt that certain powers that be looked favourably on their efforts, including countries in the Contact Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on page 33, line 15, it is stated Republic of Croatia where it should stand Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00461.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, please, Mr. Jovanovic, take a look at tab number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be 65 ter 1062, and in e-court that would be document K009-2901. That would be 65 ter of the Prosecution 4014, 4014.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, here we have joint statement of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the president of the Russian Federation dated 16th of June, 1998. Please tell us whether you took part in those talks, what was the reason for them, and what was the main point of this joint statement.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in the talks by President Slobodan Milosevic and President Boris Yeltsin on the 16th of June, 1998, in Moscow. That meeting took part at the initiative and on the invitation of Russian Federation's president Mr. Boris Yeltsin took part in the Ekaterina Hall of the Kremlin castle. It's in my opinion an important -- a very important international document, all the more important because this is not a document which ensues from run-of-the-mill bilateral meetings, but is rather a document whereby the president of the Russian Federation, Mr. Boris Yeltsin, worked on it as a member of the Contact Group, meaning that he represented the international community in those talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please offer your comments. The fifth bullet point and the attitude of Yugoslavia in terms of getting an insight in the situation.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this provides political basis for an acceptance of international civilian presence in Kosovo and Metohija, with a view to getting an insight in the situation on the ground. In practical terms, this document and this paragraph is the basis for the setting up of the KDOM mission, the Kosovo Diplomatic Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please, the penultimate and the last bullet point, if you could offer your comments on those.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since those activities and the presence in the Kosovo and Metohija area are conducted under the wing of the OSCE, Organisation For Security and Co-Operation in Europe, the two presidents stated that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was ready to start conducting negotiations with the OSCE on the reception of their mission to Kosovo and Metohija and on the restoration of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's membership in that organisation, that is, on the lifting of the suspension which was in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to admit this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00462.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we leave the document, Your Honours, could I just indicate that the English version has a date or the year being 1996. That should be corrected. I think it's a pretty obvious error, but I note it for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now if we could take a look, please, at 65 ter document 1060.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That would be tab 9 in your binder and D008-4788 in the e-court. Mr. Jovanovic, before we start working on this document which is dated 10th of July, 1998, of the SMIP point in Kosovo and Metohija, I would like to ask you this question. We heard about the efforts invested by Serbian and Yugoslav authorities to use political means to resolve the problems in Kosovo and Metohija, but what was the actual situation on the ground in June and July 1998 in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Kosovo and Metohija not only did the tensions continue because the political process had been deferred due to the rejection by the representatives of the Albanian ethnic minority of Serbia's initiatives to launch political dialogue, but also in that period terrorist activities had intensified and almost attacks with tragic consequences had become daily occurrence. Those attacks were directed at representatives of the legal institutions or civilians. In our assessment it had become apparent that the tactic being applied on the part of the representatives of political structures of the Albanians was to bide time, to create tensions, and to provoke the international community to get involved and for the matter to be internationally highlighted as broadly as possible. I cannot recall any numerical indicators, but in 1998, in the first half of 1998, there were intensive terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija, very many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, we have here according to the records of your office in Pristina the number of members, representatives of various countries in Kosovo and Metohija. My question is: What did the foreign ministry and the Government of Yugoslavia undertake after the statement issued by Yeltsin and the President of FRY, Milosevic, and what were the efforts undertaken by these diplomatic representatives?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yugoslav diplomats asserted the Moscow statement as a very significant document which needed to speed up the process of political settlement with the inclusion of international representatives by their presence in Kosovo and Metohija in view of the escalation of terrorist activities on the one hand and the obvious lack of understanding and impartiality in assessing the causes of the problem in Kosovo and Metohija in parts of the international community, the Yugoslav side and the Republic of Serbia wanted Kosovo to be fully open to representatives of other states to gain insight into the situation there. And to that effect, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, very quickly, almost simultaneously with the Moscow declaration, opened three outposts in Kosovo and Metohija, the main purpose of which was to provide logistics support to international diplomatic representatives so that they might effectively gain insight and on that basis develop an objective picture of the situation in Kosovo and Metohija. The foreign ministry outposts were opened in Pristina, Gnjilane, or Zanilove [as interpreter] close to Gnjilane, and in Kosovska Mitrovica. I wish to point out that the purpose of these outposts was to provide logistics aid and support to facilitate the work of the mission of foreign diplomatic representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Line 38 -- page 38, line 12, after the word "Gnjilane," it should say the village of Ranilug next to Gnjilane, Ranilug.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, if you haven't finished, please continue.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should like to draw your attention that within only 20 days since the agreement in Moscow, there were more than 50 foreign diplomatic representatives sent to Kosovo and Metohija from an important number of countries, I think more than ten countries. Out of those 50 diplomatic representatives, more than a third came from the United States of America. And this reflects the responsibility and openness of the Yugoslav side to enabling objective reporting and objective understanding of the problems in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the document be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00463.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could we now go on to tab 10, Mr. Jovanovic. D008-4761 in the e-court and 65 ter 1057, 1057. Mr. Jovanovic, we now have a report of the foreign ministry outpost in Pristina dated the 24th of July, 1998. Could you tell us what this document is about and what it is reporting. Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This document, Your Honour, contains a list of actual cases of terrorist attacks on various categories of persons in Kosovo and Metohija, representatives of state authorities and official institutions against citizens of Serb ethnicity, citizens of Albanian ethnicity, and citizens of other ethnicities in this multi-ethnic community within the territory of Serbia. This review covered the period from the 1st of January until the 15th of July, and we can see by category and by names of persons how many such terrorist actions and attacks were carried out and what the consequences were of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise if there is any misunderstanding. This is a list which the federal Ministry for Foreign Affairs received from the appropriate bodies of the Republic of Serbia and passed on to the outpost in Pristina in order to inform diplomatic representatives, members of the KDOM mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic, for the transcript. Let me indicate the date of this letter. It is the 24th of July, 1998, and now I should like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00464 [Realtime transcript read in error "D00646"].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, during the activities of this KDOM mission -- yes, yes, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may, a matter on the record here which I think is important. At line 25 it has a statement here attributed to Mr. Djurdjic, but this is in fact testimony from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that's being looked at, I think page 40, line 11 should be 464 rather than 646 as the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, it should be D464.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I wanted to ask you what was the situation regarding the number of these diplomatic representatives during the summer of 1998 who were members of this KDOM mission?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Yugoslav side did not limit in any way the number of foreign diplomatic representatives in Kosovo and Metohija. It is important to note that these were diplomatic representatives of foreign countries who were accredited and who were headquartered in Belgrade, but they were temporarily detached from their embassies, the embassies of their countries, and sent to Kosovo and Metohija in accordance with the Milosevic-Yeltsin Agreement. This number, as it was not limited, increased and it reflected exclusively the interest of other countries in monitoring the situation in Kosovo and Metohija. This number did not in any way depend on the will of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The number increased, but I think that it did not reach a very high level. Possibly -- I'm afraid I can't be precise about this, but what is important is that in July, 20 days after the Milosevic-Yeltsin Agreement, there were more than 50 foreign diplomatic representatives in Kosovo and Metohija. There may have been more, but the interest at the time was not greater. It increased later. And the attitude of the Yugoslav side could be seen from the fact that the ministry which I headed sent to Kosovo and Metohija between 20 and 30 diplomats from the ministry for logistic support for the foreign representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us briefly what the -- this KDOM mission in Kosovo and Metohija was designed to do?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the standpoint of the interests of the country of which I was the minister, the most important thing for us was that impartial information should be sent from Kosovo and Metohija to centres of decision making. That is the countries which had an influence over the initiation of the process of political settlement. That is why Yugoslav diplomacy and the federal state and the Republic of Serbia was keenly interested in having as many diplomatic representatives of foreign countries there as possible because we believed that this would contribute to a more objective representation of the problems in Kosovo and Metohija, and thereby could initiate and encourage the process of political settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were countries and organisations abroad provided with more objective information by those diplomats in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Federal Ministry for Foreign Affairs naturally did not have insight as to how foreign diplomatic representatives informed their embassies in Belgrade and their governments in their capitals from where they had come. Therefore, it remains for us to conclude that the reporting depended on the representatives of each country that had its diplomats in Kosovo and Metohija. Judging by the reactions of a certain number of influential countries, there was no significant improvement in their attitude towards the process of political settlement in Kosovo and Metohija. But judging by the reaction of other also influential countries, there was a positive fact and that is that the dialogue and communications were intensified through the KDOM so that there was an ever-present hope that this would, though slowly, contribute to more -- to a more objective representation of Kosovo and Metohija and in the final analysis that this would speed up a political solution. I wish to recall here that in June 1998 for Yugoslavia and Serbia there was an unexpected meeting between a senior representative of the American administration, Mr. Richard Holbrooke, with armed commanders of the terrorist KLA. This happened around the 20th of June, 1998, in the village of Junik. I do not remember many things in detail from that period, but I do remember this particular detail because this meeting between a representative of the representative of the United States and representatives of the KLA we saw as an about turn in American policy, and that meant that a terrorist organisation was being accepted by the United States as a political partner in a dialogue, that a formal and public dialogue was being established between the United States of America, the most influential country in -- globally; and a terrorist organisation. We felt then - and I personally still feel - that this was an enormous mistake by the American administration and that it was harmful not only for the political process in Kosovo and Metohija, but that it was an encouragement that terrorism elsewhere too. Because clearly there can't be any good or bad terrorists. And the 11th of September, 2001, will show how tragic failure to see the link that existed among terrorists throughout the world and the identity of their philosophy and their methods, this will be a declaration of recognition and removal of a terrorist organisation from the list of terrorist organisations to the list of liberation organisation and liberation movement. I mention this fact to illustrate that such moves had an encouraging effect on the intensification of terrorist activities against the state, against Serbia, against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, against its institutions, against its constitutional and state order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Now if we could take a look at tab 11 in your binder and that would be D008-4749 or 1053, the 65 ter for the Defence [as interpreted]. Mr. Jovanovic, we're about to see a press release issued by the information secretariat of AP Kosovo and Metohija dated 28th of July, 1998, on talks of the Vice-President of the government, Mr. Nikola Sainovic, and Ambassador Chris Hill. Prompted by this, I would like to ask you whether Serbia and Yugoslavia continued bilateral talks and negotiations with individual countries and international organisations throughout that period in 1998.

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's absolutely clear that the position of the United States of America determined the further course of action and events in Kosovo and Metohija and that the US of A had the most influence on the conduct of the separatists in Kosovo-Metohija and on the conduct of the exponents of the separatist movement. And for that reason, Yugoslavia paid utmost attention to dialogue with the United States of America, because only through such dialogue could positive breakthrough have been effected. For instance, that meeting with the terrorists in Junik, United States of America continually pressed Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and through them the leadership of Serbia to launch political dialogue and political process, but on the other hand, they would take under their wing those with whom Serbia was supposed to enter into dialogue. And the meeting of Mr. Nikola Sainovic, Vice-President of the Federal Republic, with Ambassador Chris Hill was a reflection of such take on the situation and an indicator of Yugoslavia's continued interests in essential dialogue with the United States of America in the hope that the United States of America would influence the separatist movement in Kosovo and Metohija to accept political dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00465.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, you stated that in summer of 1998 terrorist activities intensified in Kosovo and Metohija. I would like to ask you with respect to that, what was that intensification, how did it look like, and what measures were undertaken by Republic of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ZIVADIN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As has been stated on several occasions, the intensification of terrorist activities and actions was reflected in more frequent attacks on representatives of state institutions, on representatives of authorities at different levels, particularly terrorism was reflected in ambushes against policemen and other representatives of public services. Another aspect of such intensified activities and the fact that the situation in Kosovo and Metohija was growing more complicated was inability to conduct public traffic and to conduct normal economic cultural life. The circulation in terms of the economy, everyday life, cultural activities was hindered by check-points, by barricades, and a large swathe of Serbia's territory in Kosovo and Metohija came under the control of the terrorist KLA. Yugoslavia and Serbia took two types of activities. The first was to be open towards the international community for it, through its presence, to allow objective understanding of the problems in Kosovo and Metohija and to influence for an early acceptance of the initiatives offered by official institutions to find a political solution.
